docs.title: About Minirogue Build Logic
docs.text: This project is my own personal Gradle convention plugins. Note that they do not follow all recommended practices for larger teams.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
This repo manages several dependencies (namely ones that have related gradle plugins) that will be inherited by any projects that consume it. As of version 0.3.6 the following dependencies and versions are used:

  • Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) = 9.2.1
  • ComposeMultiplatform = 1.12.0
  • Detekt = 2.0.0-alpha.6
  • HotReload = 1.2.0
  • Java = 21
  • Kotlin = 2.4.10
  • Kotlin Serialization = 1.11.0
  • Kotlin Symbol Processing = 2.3.11
  • Metro = 1.4.2
  • Room = 2.8.4

Minimum supported Gradle version: 9.4.1 Latest tested Gradle version: 9.5.0

docs.title: Importing the build logic
docs.text:
This section assumes that the consuming project is a gradle project using a version catalog.

Ensure that the following is in the consuming project's settings.gradle.kts file:

pluginManagement {
    resolutionStrategy {
        eachPlugin {
            if (requested.id.toString() == "com.github.minirogue")
                useModule("com.github.minirogue:minirogue-build-logic:$requested.version")
        }
    }
    repositories {
        maven { url "https://jitpack.io" }
    }
}

Then add the following to the version catalog:

[plugins]
minirogue-plugin = { id = "com.github.minirogue", version = "0.3.6" }

and finally add the following to the root project build.gradle

plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.minirogue.plugin) apply false
}

docs.title: Applying and using the plugins
docs.text:
Then the following plugins may be used for any gradle modules contained in the project:

  • minirogue.multiplatform.library
  • minirogue.test.app
  • minirogue.android.app
  • minirogue.jvm.app

Then you may use the minirogue extension in the build.gradle file using the plugin to configure it:

minirogue {
    android()
    ios()
    metro()
}
